topic: Solar System and Earth's Interior of Geography
description: Our Solar System comprises the Sun and eight planets. The study of the Earth's interior is primarily based on indirect evidence derived from seismic waves and volcanic eruptions, as direct observation is impossible beyond a few kilometers.

sections.title: Basics of the Solar System
sections.description: Crucial facts and scientific theories regarding the formation and composition of the Sun and the universe.

key_concepts.explanation: A theory proposed by Immanuel Kant and revised by Laplace, which suggests that the solar system was formed from a giant, rotating cloud of gas and dust called a nebula.
A circumstellar disc in the Solar System located roughly between the orbits of the planets Mars and Jupiter, occupied by numerous irregularly shaped rocky bodies.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: 4 Hydrogen nuclei -> 1 Helium nucleus + Tremendous Energy
scientific_principles.application: This is the primary source of energy in the Sun and other stars, where hydrogen converts into helium under extreme temperature and pressure.

important_facts.fact: The Sun alone accounts for approximately 99.8% of the total mass of our entire Solar System.
Light Year and Parsec are units used to measure vast astronomical distances, not time. 1 Parsec is equal to 3.26 Light Years.

sections.title: Classification and Characteristics of Planets
sections.description: The eight planets of the solar system are divided into two main categories based on their physical composition and proximity to the Sun.

key_concepts.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. They are made up of rocks and metals, possess solid surfaces, and have relatively high densities.
Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. They are massive gas giants with thick atmospheres, mostly made of hydrogen and helium, and have low densities.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the hottest planet in the solar system due to an intense greenhouse effect. It is also known as the 'Morning Star', 'Evening Star', and 'Earth's Twin'.
The largest planet with the fastest rotation speed (completes one rotation in about 10 hours). It is famous for the 'Great Red Spot', a giant storm.

key_associations.extra_info: These are the two small, irregularly shaped natural satellites (moons) of Mars.
Saturn's largest moon, unique for being the only moon in the solar system with a dense atmosphere.
The largest and most massive natural satellite in our Solar System, even larger than the planet Mercury.

sections.title: Interior Layers of the Earth
sections.description: Based on chemical composition and physical properties, the Earth's interior is divided into three primary concentric layers.

key_concepts.explanation: The outermost, solid, and thinnest layer. The continental crust is primarily composed of Silica and Aluminum (SIAL), while the oceanic crust consists of Silica and Magnesium (SIMA).

The thickest layer located just below the crust. Its upper portion is highly viscous and is called the Asthenosphere (weak zone), which is the primary source of magma that finds its way to the surface.
The innermost layer, composed mainly of heavy metals like Nickel and Iron (NIFE). The outer core is in a liquid state, whereas the inner core is solid due to extreme gravitational pressure.

important_facts.fact: The average radius of the Earth is approximately 6371 kilometers.
The average density of the Earth is 5.51 g/cm³, which makes it the densest planet in the Solar System.

sections.title: Discontinuities inside the Earth
sections.description: Transition zones or boundaries between the various layers of the Earth where seismic waves abruptly change their velocity.

key_associations.extra_info: Marks the transition based on the difference in density and composition.
The most frequently asked boundary in competitive exams, discovered by Andrija Mohorovicic.
Located at a depth of about 700 km, marking a change in mineral structure.
A major boundary where S-waves completely disappear, indicating a phase change from solid to liquid.
Separates the liquid outer core from the solid inner core.

sections.title: Seismic Waves and Evidences
sections.description: The study of seismic waves generated during earthquakes provides the most reliable and authentic source of information about the Earth's interior.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Longitudinal compressional waves, analogous to sound waves.
scientific_principles.application: They are the fastest seismic waves and can travel through all mediums (solid, liquid, and gaseous). Their velocity decreases in liquids.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Transverse shear waves, analogous to light waves or water ripples.
scientific_principles.application: They can travel ONLY through solid mediums. Their inability to pass through the outer core is the primary proof that the outer core is liquid.

key_concepts.explanation: Specific areas on the Earth's surface where seismographs cannot detect certain seismic waves from a given earthquake. The zone between 105 degrees and 145 degrees from the epicenter is a common shadow zone for both P and S waves.
